instrument: Watchdog, kennel main 6a05dfb6c, rubric-2026.10.1; contained scans (codehealth-analyzer:train-src-89d1e8def87553cc)
headline: contained scan, scanner default configuration

falseNegativeMechanisms.title: No rule for the concept at all (scanner-neutral concepts beyond the reference scanner: unmapped or unevidenced in the mapping)
Repository-wide posture switches: one qualifying site anywhere credits the whole repository, so the defective site is never itemised (P7, P8, C2, S1, D40, D42, P10, P11, P6)

Code-health and test rules with no TypeScript arm (suppressions, commented-out code, empty catch, dead private code, @deprecated use, catch-rethrow, null dereference, swallowed test failures, mock dominance)

Pattern recognisers too shallow for the defect's shape (.Result, Assert.True(true), WarningsNotAsErrors, eslint config off-switches, Error('Not implemented'), hollow methods, density bars, bare floating promises, inert options, undrained stderr, vitest test without expect, truncation loops)

Prefix-less secrets: every vendor-prefixed secret was found, every secret without a vendor prefix was missed (punctuated Password=, credentials in connection URIs, inline Bearer, unquoted dotenv, .http files, Vite define)
Injection taint confined to the request handler: the tainted value arrives as a method parameter, model-bound argument, component state or ternary, or passes a function assumed safe (path.join)

Injection sink or library with no rule in the baked packs (Dapper, EF FromSqlRaw, Newtonsoft TypeNameHandling, ContentResult XSS, Redirect, Regex without timeout, MongoDB filters, dynamic RegExp, log injection, Blazor MarkupString)

Architecture / domain detectors read too narrow a population (project-reference cycles only, test edges in instability, no pass-through detection, attributes and projections ignored, entities without Id, declared references excuse co-change, test-support project not seen as test code)

Measured but never reported: per-site rows at Info/Recommendation level or below a score threshold never reach SARIF; only a location-less roll-up does (X2 CancellationToken, D12/npm outdated, R7 unused exports, R3 size)

Data-flow rules that match call NAMES, not data: source-generated [LoggerMessage] methods, structured log fields, headers inside a logged object, localStorage under a neutral key, MD5.HashData / createHash('md5') for passwords
DM9-DM11 have no TypeScript arm, and DM6/DM7 only partial ones (decorators only; no interface type arguments)
Found the file, missed the site: checkov/trivy Kubernetes rows at line 1 or the pod spec, a duplicate-block window that starts early, a misplaced dependency reported at its importer
Model-judged accessibility text cards (LA2 alt text, LA5 link text, LA6 labels) are composed only with a compliance framework configured, so the default configuration measures nothing
Dependency hygiene arms missing: npm deprecation not graded, EOL ignores engines.node and nested packages, R8 unused/undeclared blind on TypeScript
Presence-only runtime checks: X2 checks that a token parameter exists, not that it is forwarded; an injected fetch hides outbound HTTP from P7/X2; Console output is neither a log call nor flagged
ADR / documentation conformance is model-judged: absent from contained scans and unreliable in host passes (prose-enforced ADRs, README drift, ADR contradicted by an endpoint)
AC6 reads <style> blocks and inline styles only: motion and focus-outline defects in .css / .razor.css files are invisible
Flaky tests: detection is three re-runs (a 1e-4 flake never shows), no time-zone/clock-read rule, the fixed-sleep rule reads C# only
IaC / CI checks absent in the pinned rule sets: Ingress without TLS, pull_request_target checking out and building the PR head

top.mechanism: D23 'Cross-context type X (A -> B) ... exposed in B's public surface ... couples the contexts' derives a type's bounded context from its PROJECT/assembly, so a context's own Domain types used by its own Application layer, integration events from the published Contracts project, and the shared messaging kernel are all reported as cross-context coupling.

M4 'README/code drift' publishes rows that come straight from the model's reading of the README ('reported by the model that read the README against this repository; no term search was run for this one, so nothing here has been checked against the tree') — an unverified claim is emitted as a finding.

The TS coverage run installs with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, which skips native-binding install steps (libxmljs2's prebuilt binding); every suite that imports the application then fails to load, and D8 publishes per-file 'Low coverage: 0.0%' rows for the whole route layer as a fact about the repository instead of degrading the measurement.

ED3 'Event not named in past tense' and DM3 'Integration event couples to a producer-owned domain type' classify HTTP request/response records and contract summary DTOs (types under a *.Contracts namespace/folder) as events, although nothing publishes them.

D21 (model-judged naming consistency) emits rows whose text concludes 'These are distinct operations ... No inconsistency.: No change needed.' — the model's negative verdicts are published as findings.

M4 checks a README feature claim by matching model-chosen phrases ('CSV import functionality in CLI', 'typescript-eslint strict', 'React hooks rules') against file and directory NAMES and manifest text; when the phrase is not a name the implemented feature is reported as missing.

D5 'Off the main sequence' publishes a finding for every concrete, stable library (domain core, application layer, contracts) with distance >= 0.7, including rows whose own text says 'the shape a shared-kernel / building-block library has BY DESIGN' — a row that concedes the shape is healthy is still emitted.

D17 'AnalyzerSeverityNone' reports a `dotnet_diagnostic.<id>.severity = none` line in .editorconfig as an undocumented, repository-wide suppression ('the only record that it was ever switched off is this line') even when the comment on the line directly above states the reason and a nested src/.editorconfig re-enables the rule for all production code.

D24 model-judged 'redundant comment' asks to remove grouping headings inside long registration methods ('// Persistence', '// E-mail and reminders') and comments stating a physical purpose the code cannot express.

R10 'Duplicated block (7 lines x 2 locations)' / 'with local edits' / 'concentrated across sibling directories' reports 5-10 line parallel accessors, shared call preludes (parse, look up, stop on a miss) and a 10-line HTML escaper duplicated across two separately compiled targets, where extraction would add indirection without removing a maintenance risk.

D8 ('Low coverage: 0.0%') and R4 ('No test reaches this file') report composition roots, process entry points, release scripts and thin browser glue over vendor SDKs as untested; the reachability/coverage fact is right, but the implied 'must be unit-tested' does not apply to wiring files whose collaborators are each tested.
